identity.title: Machine Learning meets Algebraic Combinatorics: A Suite of Datasets Capturing Research-level Conjecturing Ability in Pure Mathematics

problem.claim: Enable machine-learning systems to engage with research-level, open-ended conjecturing in algebraic combinatorics.

gap.claim: Existing mathematics resources are much less common at the difficulty and open-endedness of professional mathematicians’ open problems.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Algebraic Combinatorics Dataset Repository (ACD Repo), comprising nine datasets covering foundational results or open problems.
Frames each dataset around an open-ended research-level question paired with up to 10M examples from which conjectures should be generated.
Describes possible machine-learning applications and challenges in designing research-level conjecturing datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The collection is distinguished by targeting the conjecturing process and by focusing on research-level algebraic-combinatorics questions with large example sets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the repository contains nine datasets.
The authors report that individual datasets include example collections reaching up to 10M cases in some instances.
The authors report example application routes including narrow-model training followed by interpretability analysis and LLM-based program synthesis.

narrative_sequence.summary: Growing AI capabilities have increased interest in machine learning for reasoning-heavy mathematical tasks.
Available mathematics resources rarely match professional-level open-ended problems.
The paper introduces ACD Repo for foundational results and open problems in algebraic combinatorics.
The datasets target conjecture generation from open-ended questions and large collections of examples.
The paper surveys all nine datasets, application strategies, and dataset-design challenges.

source_observation.claim: The datasets pair an open-ended research question with many examples and explicitly target conjecture generation.

lessons.interpretation: This aligns benchmark inputs with the actual structure of an exploratory reasoning task rather than only testing fixed-answer problem solving.
lessons.application: For a new reasoning benchmark, define the desired discovery activity explicitly and provide examples intended to support that activity.
lessons.exception: This design may be unsuitable when the target capability is formal verification, closed-form answering, or another task with a fixed output criterion.

unknowns: The abstract reports no measured model performance, baseline comparisons, or evaluation protocol.
It does not specify the contents, provenance, or task-level metrics of the nine datasets.
